name: a-shared-big-buffer-hides-over-reads
why: parse() gets a pointer into a large reused buffer: a read past the end of the input stays inside the buffer, and no sanitizer notices.

edits.old:
const Bytes copy = input;
    return parse(copy.data(), copy.size());

name: no-round-trip
why: only crashes are looked for: no property is checked, no empty packet is tried.

name: no-prefixes
why: the messages are never cut short.

name: property-never-stops-the-program
why: a violated property is only printed: the program still ends normally.

name: a-fuzz-test-that-crashes-on-good-code
why: the fuzz test itself must survive the real parser.

name: no-make-packet
why: the inputs are never built with make_packet (Clean tier): it is the only structure-aware generator.

edits.old: const ParseResult empty = parse_exact(make_packet({}));  // the smallest packet: A5 00 00
edits.new: const ParseResult empty = parse_exact(Bytes{kMagic, 0, 0});  // the smallest packet: A5 00 00
